item.title: Burger King is testing AI headsets that will know if employees say “welcome” or “thank you”
item.description: Burger King is testing AI-powered headsets that can recite recipes, alert managers when inventories are low and even track how friendly employees are to customers.

item.title: Young woman says she was on social media ‘all day long’ as a child in landmark addiction trial
item.description: A 20-year-old woman is seeking to hold social media companies responsible for harms to children who use their platforms.

item.title: Bill Clinton says he ‘did nothing wrong’ with Epstein as he faces grilling over their relationship
item.description: Former President Bill Clinton has told members of Congress he “did nothing wrong” in his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and saw no signs of Epstein's sexual abuse.

item.title: US military used laser to take down Border Protection drone, lawmakers say
item.description: Members of Congress say the U.S. military used a laser to shoot down a Customs and Border Protection drone.

item.title: 30 years after Pokémon’s release, fans are still trying to catch ’em all
item.description: Pokemon celebrated its 30th anniversary on Friday after years of communities trading cards, watching the show and playing games.

item.title: NASA overhauls its Artemis program to return astronauts to the moon
item.description: NASA said Friday it’s adding an extra moon mission by Artemis astronauts before attempting a high-risk lunar landing with a crew.

item.title: Attorney general announces indictment against 30 more people who protested at a Minnesota church
item.description: Attorney General Pam Bondi says federal prosecutors have indicted 30 more people tied to a protest at a Minnesota church over an immigration enforcement crackdown.

item.title: Teenage girls are most likely to tear their ACLs. Parents say more must be done to protect them
item.description: Girl's who play high school sports suffer ACL injuries at much higher rates than their male counterparts, researchers say — up to eight times more likely.

item.title: Target will stop selling cereals with synthetic colors by end of May
item.description: Target said Friday it's been phasing out synthetic colors in cereals for years. Right now, 85% of its cereal sales come from products made without synthetic dyes.

item.title: Convicted murderer apprehended after escape from federal custody in Utah
item.description: A Utah man convicted of murder, aggravated sexual assault and fraud, among several other crimes, has been apprehended after failing to return to a federal halfway house in Salt Lake City last month.
